mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by at least 0.25 percentage points over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected equity returns, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥ 0.25 pp in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified rate hike episode (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by non-equity factors.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months signals disinflation, which reduces market expectations of future rate hikes and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥ 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the identified disinflation episode (t-test p ≥ 0.05), or CPIAUCSL reaccelerates before the return window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs in a single month coincides with rising labor market confidence, which accelerates corporate investment and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 10,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat during the identified employment surge (mean p-value > 0.05 across 5 backtests).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) unexpectedly exceeds its prior month by at least 2% and coincides with rising retail sales (HOUST) by ≥ 5%, it signals resilient demand momentum that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥ 2% AND HOUST increases by ≥ 5% relative to prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the identified demand pattern (t-test p ≥ 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% for two months suggests tight labor markets, prompting firms to accelerate capex and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the two-month tight labor regime (mean p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail activity (HOUST) of at least 8% in a single month, following a prior month of expansion, indicates a demand pullback that depresses equity valuations and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥ 8% in a month after a prior month of increase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during the identified cooling episode (t-test p ≥ 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent increases in the monthly RSAFS index of financial market activity by at least 15% over three consecutive months suggest heightened risk appetite and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by ≥ 15% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the identified risk-on episode (mean p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals a softening labor market, which typically coincides with equity valuation compression and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases above 6.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the identified labor market weakening (mean p-value > 0.05).
